notes: Mode-A golden set for decision_conditions.extract_conditions (fund-grade S5). Each case is a 'What would change my mind' section body + the ticker's metric vocabulary; expected pins the graded fields (metric, metric_source, op, threshold, unit, for_periods) — `note` is freeform and ungraded. Order-insensitive compare; score = matched / max(n_expected, n_actual).

kpi_names: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk)
cases.section: Two prints would flip this call. First, 90d+ NPLs pushing above 7% for two consecutive quarters would mean the credit book is deteriorating faster than the yield compensates. Second, monthly ARPAC falling below $10 would break the monetization leg of the thesis.

Subscription revenue growth dropping below 20% YoY for 2 consecutive quarters would tell me the AI-consumption story is not converting into bookings, and I would exit the position rather than wait for margin offsets.

The capex super-cycle is tolerable only while cash generation holds. Quarterly free cash flow printing below $1.5B would change my mind — at that level the buyback math and the AI-spend runway both break.
If cost-to-serve rises to $1.20 or above for three straight quarters, the operating-leverage thesis is broken regardless of what customer growth does.
Cloud backlog conversion dropping under 30% would signal that the RPO build is bookings theater rather than future revenue, and I would cut the position.

A change of CEO, a credible activist campaign against the holdco structure, or a regulatory move against carried-interest taxation would each force a rethink — none of these is a number I can watch on a dashboard, but any would change my mind.

Two things. Credit NPLs above 25% would mean the fintech book is repeating the 2022 mistake — that is checkable every quarter. And a major devaluation in Argentina would hurt, though the timing and size of that is not something I can put a threshold on.

Risk-adjusted NIM compressing by more than 200bps year-over-year — a print of -200bps or worse on the YoY change — for two quarters running would mean funding costs are outrunning yield and the spread story is over.
